questions.q: A business user asks you to informally grant them access to a dataset classified as restricted. What does this lesson say is the right response?
options: Follow the documented access request and approval process rather than granting access because someone asked
Grant it immediately since the user already knows the data exists
Refuse to ever discuss access requests with business users
Grant access only if the user is a manager, regardless of role or process
questions.explain: Access decisions for sensitive data follow a documented, role-based approval process. Granting access informally bypasses the control that governance exists to enforce.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the practical difference between masking and encryption that an interviewer is testing for?
options: Masking hides a value in use (such as for non-production visibility), while encryption protects data at rest or in transit — and policy decides which applies where
Masking and encryption are two names for the exact same technique
Encryption is only used for passwords, never for other sensitive fields
Masking is a stronger protection than encryption in every case
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes masking (hiding a value during use or limited-visibility scenarios) from encryption (protecting data at rest or in transit), with a governance policy — not a single tool — deciding which applies to a given dataset.

questions.q: What is a data subject access request, and what is a governance analyst's typical role in handling one?
options: A person's request to know, correct, or delete data held about them — the governance analyst typically coordinates the process rather than personally executing every technical step
A request only software engineers are allowed to submit
A one-time report generated automatically with no human involvement
A request that only applies to employee data, never customer data
questions.explain: A data subject access request is a person's request regarding their own personal data. The governance analyst usually knows where the data lives and coordinates the response, rather than personally deleting or correcting every record.

questions.q: What is a model card, as described in this lesson?
options: A structured document describing a model's purpose, training data, and known limitations — the AI-governance equivalent of a data dictionary entry
A physical ID card issued to data scientists
A credit score used to approve machine learning budgets
A marketing one-pager advertising a model's accuracy to customers
questions.explain: A model card documents a model's purpose, training data, and limitations, functioning for AI governance the way a data dictionary entry functions for a regular dataset.

questions.q: When a business team wants to use a generative AI tool on customer data, what does this lesson recommend checking first?
options: The data's classification — whether it's allowed to leave its current environment at all — before considering vendor terms and output review
Nothing; approval should be automatic as long as the team asks nicely
Only the cost of the AI tool's subscription
Whether the tool's name sounds trustworthy
questions.explain: The lesson's sample answer confirms data classification first, then loops in security and legal on vendor data-handling terms, and requires human review of outputs — in that order of priority.
